Benchmarking Screening Methods: Classification Accuracy

Source: vignettes/Benchmark_Accuracy.Rmd
Benchmark_Accuracy.Rmd
library(SigBridgeR)
library(Seurat)

Overview

BenchAcc() compute the classification accuracy of screening methods according to a known ground truth

It treats "Positive" as the positive class and every other supported label ("Negative", "Neutral", "Other") as the negative class. For each screening method found in the object, it computes a full set of binary classification metrics, so the methods can be ranked or compared on exactly the same cells.

The function accepts three kinds of input:

  • a Seurat object whose meta.data contains one column per screening method;
  • a ScreenMethodResult, which is unwrapped to its scRNA_data slot;
  • a BenchAccConfig, which runs every configured screening method first and then evaluates the merged labels in one pass.

A small example

The example below uses a tiny object with six cells, a ground-truth column and two simulated screening results. In a real analysis the Scissor and scPAS columns would be produced by Screen() or MergeResult().

counts <- Matrix::Matrix(
  matrix(
    seq_len(24L),
    nrow = 4L,
    dimnames = list(paste0("Gene", 1:4), paste0("Cell", 1:6))
  ),
  sparse = TRUE
)

sc <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = counts)

sc$truth <- c(
  "Positive",
  "Negative",
  "Positive",
  "Other",
  "Positive",
  "Negative"
)
sc$Scissor <- c(
  "Positive",
  "Negative",
  "Positive",
  "Other",
  "Negative",
  "Negative"
)
sc$scPAS <- c(
  "Positive",
  "Positive",
  "Negative",
  "Other",
  "Negative",
  "Negative"
)

metrics <- BenchAcc(sc, bench_config = "truth", verbose = FALSE)

round(do.call(rbind, metrics), 3)
#>           TPR   FPR   TNR   FNR  F1 Accuracy Precision Recall
#> Scissor 0.667 0.000 1.000 0.333 0.8    0.833       1.0  0.667
#> scPAS   0.333 0.333 0.667 0.667 0.4    0.500       0.5  0.333

Each element of the returned list is a one-row matrix whose row name is the screening method. The same numbers are easier to compare after binding them:

metrics_dt <- data.table::rbindlist(
  lapply(metrics, as.data.frame),
  idcol = "method"
)

metrics_dt[, .(method, TPR, FPR, F1, Accuracy, Precision, Recall)]
#>     method       TPR       FPR    F1  Accuracy Precision    Recall
#>     <char>     <num>     <num> <num>     <num>     <num>     <num>
#> 1: Scissor 0.6666667 0.0000000   0.8 0.8333333       1.0 0.6666667
#> 2:   scPAS 0.3333333 0.3333333   0.4 0.5000000       0.5 0.3333333

Specifying the ground truth

bench_config can be given in two equivalent forms:

# * a length-one column name in sc@meta.data
from_column <- BenchAcc(sc, bench_config = "truth", verbose = FALSE)

# * a per-cell label vector, one label per cell
from_vector <- BenchAcc(sc, bench_config = sc$truth, verbose = FALSE)

identical(from_column, from_vector)
#> [1] TRUE

The labels must contain "Positive", and the vector form must have one element per cell. The function stops with an informative error when the column is missing, when the labels have no positive class, or when the vector length does not match the number of cells:

BenchAcc(sc, bench_config = "missing_column", verbose = FALSE)
#> Error in `BenchAcc()`:
#> ✖ "missing_column" is not a valid column name in obj@meta.data

Reading the metrics

With PP positive and NN negative ground-truth cells, and TPTP, FPFP, TNTN, FNFN the usual confusion-matrix counts, BenchAcc() reports:

Metric Definition Meaning
TPR / Recall TP/(TP+FN)TP / (TP + FN) Fraction of truly positive cells recovered
FPR FP/(FP+TN)FP / (FP + TN) Fraction of negative cells incorrectly called positive
TNR TN/(TN+FP)TN / (TN + FP) Fraction of negative cells correctly left out
FNR FN/(FN+TP)FN / (FN + TP) Fraction of positive cells missed
Precision TP/(TP+FP)TP / (TP + FP) Fraction of called cells that are truly positive
F1 2TP/(2TP+FP+FN)2TP / (2TP + FP + FN) Harmonic mean of precision and recall
Accuracy (TP+TN)/(P+N)(TP + TN) / (P + N) Overall agreement with the ground truth

Because screening methods usually return only a small positive set, Accuracy tends to be high and similar across methods. TPR/Recall, Precision and F1 are usually more informative when comparing methods. A method that selects very few cells can have perfect precision but low recall, while a permissive method can have high recall but many false positives.

BenchAcc() only scores screening method columns. Other metadata columns, including the ground-truth column itself, are ignored. Method names are matched case-insensitively against the methods registered in ScreenStrategy:

sc$SCISSOR <- sc$Scissor
sc$Scissor <- NULL

names(BenchAcc(sc, bench_config = "truth", verbose = FALSE))
#> [1] "scPAS"   "SCISSOR"

Benchmarking the screening step

If the screening has not been run yet, wrap the inputs in a BenchAccConfig. The configuration stores the bulk data, the single-cell object, the phenotype and the methods to run. BenchAcc() then screens the data with each method and evaluates the accumulated labels:

config <- BenchAccConfig(
  matched_bulk = bulk,
  sc_data = sc,
  phenotype = phenotype,
  label_type = "{method_name}",
  phenotype_class = "binary",
  screen_method = c("Scissor", "scPAS"),
  method_param = MethodParamSet(
    Scissor_param = list(alpha = 0.05),
    scPAS_param = list(alpha = 0.01)
  ),
  bench_config = "truth"
)

acc <- BenchAcc(config, verbose = FALSE)

The bench_config of a BenchAccConfig is validated when the object is created, so an invalid ground truth fails early instead of after a long screening run. method_param is the place for method-specific arguments; see ?MethodParamSet for the full list of fields.

Practical notes

  • Use the same cells for every method. BenchAcc() compares the labels cell by cell. Merge the screening results first (for example with MergeResult()) so that every method shares the same cell names and order.
  • Use an independent ground truth. A label derived from the same bulk phenotype that drove the screening is not an independent validation; use marker-based annotation, an external cell-type reference or held-out experimental labels when possible.
  • Report more than accuracy. TPR, Precision and F1 describe the trade-off between missing positive cells and including negative ones, which is usually the relevant question for phenotype-associated cell screening.
  • Only the four supported labels are accepted. Predicted labels must be one of "Positive", "Negative", "Neutral" or "Other"; typos and NA abort with the offending column and row.

See also

  • BenchGSEA() for comparing the functional signal of the selected cells.
  • BenchGeneScore() for comparing pathway activity at the single-cell level.
  • BenchMemory() for comparing run time and memory.
  • BenchAccConfig(), MethodParamSet() and ?Screen for the configuration and screening interfaces.
